jobs.title: Director, Process Transformation and Optimization
jobs.description:
Description

Build the future with us

Would you like to contribute directly to the evolution of the company’s operating model and play a key role in sustainably improving its performance?

As Director, Process Transformation and Optimization, you will lead the corporate capabilities that enable us to simplify ways of working, increase organizational capacity, and transform work in the age of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.

You will contribute to strengthening the organization’s ability to rethink its processes and business system by leveraging AI, automation, and emerging technologies. You will lead managers and expert teams responsible for process transformation, enterprise productivity, AI-driven optimization, and the evolution of operating models.

______________________________________________________________________________

What You’ll Accomplish With Us

As Director, Process Transformation and Optimization, you will be at the heart of our mission. Your main responsibilities will include:

Define the corporate vision, direction, and priorities for process transformation and the evolution of the business system.
Anticipate trends that are transforming the way we work and evolve corporate transformation methods, standards, tools, and capabilities.
Recommend priorities for action to senior leadership based on their strategic impact, transformation potential, and contribution to sustainable productivity improvement.
Influence senior leaders and governance bodies to accelerate the transformations required to achieve the company’s ambitions.
Lead the evolution of the corporate enterprise productivity framework, including performance indicators and a consolidated view of organizational capacity, productivity, and potential gains.
Lead and prioritize portfolios of initiatives involving diagnostics, optimization, re-engineering, transformation, and strategic workshops, while developing reusable corporate assets and facilitating knowledge transfer to business units.
Define the engagement model and commitments with business units and subsidiaries, assume accountability for results, and lead, engage, and develop the managers and teams under your responsibility.

______________________________________________________________________________

What Could Accelerate Your Success In This Role

We are looking for someone who:

Holds a master’s degree in business administration, project management, industrial engineering, operations management, information systems, or a related field.
Has significant experience in process transformation, productivity, or operating model evolution within complex organizations.
Has strong knowledge of re-engineering, simplification, continuous improvement, and systemic diagnostic approaches.
Has a practical understanding of AI, automation, and emerging technologies, as well as their impact on processes, work, roles, and controls.
Demonstrates the ability to lead specialized teams and prioritize a portfolio of requests.
Stands out through strategic leadership, systems thinking, and the ability to mobilize senior leaders around large-scale transformations.
Demonstrates a strong focus on productivity, measurable results, and sustaining long-term gains.
Advanced proficiency in French is required, as well as an intermediate level of English, as the incumbent will be required to participate in meetings, exchange emails, prepare and present documents, and deliver presentations to unilingual English-speaking business partners within a French-speaking team.

______________________________________________________________________________

Why you’ll love working with us

A work environment where learning and development come together with a shared pursuit of excellence;
Artificial intelligence is in everyone’s hands, helping you increase your personal effectiveness while supporting the organization’s growth;
A healthy, safe, equitable, and inclusive environment where everyone has the opportunity to reach their full potential and grow;
The opportunity to work in a hybrid environment supported by flexibility and access to inspiring and innovative workspaces.

______________________________________________________________________________

Competitive Benefits

Flexible group insurance
Competitive pension plan
Employee share purchase plan
Vacation, well-being, and personal development days
Telemedicine
Employee and family assistance program
Ergonomic office furniture program
Performance bonus
Discounts on iA products
And more!

______________________________________________________________________________

Apply now and take the lead in your career, where your talent truly matters!

______________________________________________________________________________

Not sure whether to apply?

At iA, we believe in potential and value diverse experiences. If this role inspires you, take the leap and apply. Your place may be with us, and we want to get to know you!

jobs.title: Director of Finance- Agentic
jobs.description:
Open to Canada and Latin America - Working EST timezone

We're Search Atlas, an agentic marketing platform. We combine SEO, content, site management and AI automation into one system.

We are looking for a Director of Finance who owns the finance function, leads the team, and makes clear calls. If you want real ownership, move fast, and raise the bar every week, keep reading. If you wait to be told what to do, this isn't the role.

This role is Agentic

You build your own AI agents and automations, and use them every day to do real finance work: run analysis, automate the close, reconcile accounts and build reports. Any tool works, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc. The key is that you built the agents and automations yourself. We’ll look at this closely in the assessment and interviews.

What you'll own

Build AI agents and automations that run our finance work:
the close, reconciliations and reporting, and teach the team to do the same.
Lead the finance team and own the function end to end.
Make clear ownership calls so every task has one accountable person.
Close the books every month across multiple entities: P&L, balance sheet and cash flow.
Lead the move from cash to accrual accounting, including revenue recognition for subscriptions and refunds.
Keep Stripe and QuickBooks in sync and the books ready for audit.
Give leadership clear forecasts, cash reporting and SaaS metrics: ARR, NRR, churn.
Work with our US CPA firm on tax.

What we're looking for

You've built your own AI agents and automations for real work
, using tools like Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. We'll ask you to show us
.
6+ years in finance, with experience leading a team
Experience owning P&L reporting across multiple entities
Deep QuickBooks Online skills
Strong with SaaS metrics: ARR, NRR, churn
Experience with Stripe reconciliation and US GAAP
You speak up, make decisions, and don't wait to be told what to do.

Nice to have

CPA or CA
Experience at a SaaS company between $10M and $50M ARR

You'll thrive here if...

You lead the team and do the work yourself.
You know what matters, what can wait, and when to push back.
A fully reconciled month makes you happy. We won't judge.
Deadlines don't rattle you. Ambiguity doesn't either.
You communicate clearly, especially when things are unclear.
You can laugh at a chaotic week on Friday and mean it.

What working here actually looks like

High expectations. Real ownership. Things change fast and we don't apologize for it. You'll work with smart people who push you, a product that keeps getting better, and a team that's genuinely building something new.
We'll probably give you more to own than you expected. That's on purpose.
We use AI every day, across every function. That's just how we work.

About Search Atlas

We're the all-in-one agentic marketing platform, AI-native from day one. Our tools help marketing teams move faster, make smarter decisions, and do more with less. We're defining a new category and we're looking for people who want to be part of it.

jobs.title: Director, Global Functions Financial Control
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

This key leadership role within the Corporate Support Financial Control team reports to the VP, Corporate Support Controller. You will lead a team across three strategic mandates: financial control and governance for Global Functions, finance support for RBC's private equity portfolio, and enterprise-wide fixed assets governance through the Fixed Assets Centre of Excellence. This role sits at the intersection of controls and governance, operational excellence, and strategic business enablement. Leading this team, you will be a trusted finance partner to senior stakeholders, shaping the control environment and mentoring a high-performing team.

What will you do?

Lead a team of finance professionals responsible for financial control, reporting and governance across Global Functions, Private Equity and the Fixed Assets Centre of Excellence.
Oversee the integrity and accuracy of financial results, ensuring compliance with IFRS, RBC accounting policies and internal control requirements.
Act as a trusted finance partner to senior stakeholders across the organization, providing strategic advice, financial insights and guidance on complex accounting matters.
Provide oversight and financial control support for RBC's Global Functions, including Corporate Real Estate, Human Resources, Brand & Marketing, Group Risk Management, and the CFO Group.
Lead finance activities for RBC's Private Equity portfolio, including investment accounting, valuations, financial reporting and related governance processes.
Oversee the enterprise-wide Fixed Assets Centre of Excellence, driving consistent accounting practices, effective controls and continuous improvement across fixed asset and internally developed software (IDS) processes.
Partner with cross-functional teams to lead process improvements, system implementations, and operational transformation initiatives.
Drive operational excellence through process standardization, automation and the enhancement of financial controls and reporting capabilities.
Provide oversight and strategic direction for the team's control environment, working with the SOX office and auditors to ensure compliance with audit requirements.
Develop and mentor a high-performing team, fostering accountability, collaboration, technical expertise and professional growth.
Effectively manage and develop a team of finance professionals to foster a high-performance culture.
Lead special projects and initiatives as assigned by the VP, Corporate Support Controller.

What do you need to succeed?

Must-haves

CPA or equivalent accounting designation.
7+ years of experience in a financial control role.
Strong people management skills, with experience leading and developing a high-performing team of finance professionals.
Strong financial and analytical skills, with a solid background in accounting policy, IFRS and internal controls.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a strategic, process-improvement mindset to advise senior stakeholders on complex accounting matters.
Experience leading process improvements, automation or system implementations in a finance environment.

Nice-to-haves

Experience with RBC's financial systems.
Experience with financial control for corporate functions.
Experience managing investment accounting or valuations, ideally for private equity or similar portfolios

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in an agile, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
The opportunity to interface with senior level executives from many different parts of the organization

Job Skills

Accountability, Accounting, Accounting Finance, Communication, Continuous Improvement, Decision Making, Financial Control, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), Financial Reporting and Analysis, Leadership, Oral Communications, Strategic Thinking, Team Management, Time Management

Job Information

Job Title: Director, Financial Operations & Projects

Job Requisition ID: 89324

Ministry: Advanced Education

Location: Edmonton

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 30, 2026

Classification: Senior Manager Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 to $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135- $170,333/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Ministry Of Advanced Education

The Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta is responsible for overseeing the post-secondary education system. It plays a vital role in supporting universities, colleges, polytechnic institutions, and apprenticeship programs across the province.

In addition, the Ministry works to align education with the needs of Alberta’s economy by promoting skills development, research, and innovation. It collaborates with educational institutions, industry partners, and communities to prepare students for successful careers and to contribute to the province’s economic and social growth.

Overall, the Ministry of Advanced Education plays a critical role in shaping Alberta’s future by strengthening its workforce and supporting lifelong learning opportunities for all residents.

To learn more about the Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta and what it has to offer, follow this link: Advanced Education | Alberta.ca

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Executive Director, Financial Services, the Director, Financial Operations & Projects, leads and continuously improves the Ministry’s financial and procurement operations, systems, and processes to support strategic business objectives.

Working in a complex and evolving environment, the Director manages competing priorities, develops innovative solutions, and adapts strategies to achieve results. The role requires strong leadership, problem-solving, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills to balance interests and build consensus.

The Director provides advice and guidance to senior management, executives, the Deputy Minister, and the Minister, influencing decisions and ensuring alignment between Ministry and Government priorities. Sound judgement, diplomacy, and the ability to navigate politically and financially sensitive issues are essential.

Job Responsilbilites

Lead the Financial Operations & Projects team in the review of current systems, processes and procedures with a Save view to assessing the potential risk of the current controls and providing options for the enhancements that could be implemented to strengthen the financial controls protecting Ministry assets as well as protecting the integrity of its financial reporting controls.
Work with program areas across the department to support procurement and contracting by assessing risks, providing alternatives and identifying business solutions that meet program area needs within the parameters of prudent business and government policies and trade agreements.
Recommend options and actions to improve affordability, value for money, and alignment with government priorities.
Develop ministry-wide financial operation processes to facilitate the efficient and effective delivery of department business.
Develop innovative approaches to new and existing financial systems, and support program financial teams.
Ensure all Ministry users have access to the required automated tools and privileges to perform their duties effectively and efficiently while balancing internal controls and segregation of duties.
Manage human resource issues (e.g., recruitment, performance management, professional development plans, and supervision).
Promote a cooperative attitude between Financial Services and program areas to ensure that the review of internal controls are completed to improve the financial and procurement processes and reduce risk in the programs and divisions of the Ministry.
Provide financial advice and guidance to all levels of line management throughout the Ministry, assisting them to resolve complex management issues and ensuring that they comply with Treasury Board, Service Alberta and internal AE policies.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Drive for Results
- The position takes and delegates responsibility for outcomes, uses variety of resources to monitor own performance standards, acknowledges even indirect responsibility, commits to what is good for Albertans even if not immediately accepted and reaches goals consistent with APS direction.

Creative Problem Solving
- The position engages the community and resources at hand to address issues, engages perspective to seek root causes, finds ways to improve complex systems, employs resources from other areas to solve problems and engages others and encourages debate and idea generation to solve problems while addressing risks.

Agility
- The position identifies and manages required change and the associated risks, identifies alternative approaches and supports others to do the same, proactively explains impact of changes, anticipates and mitigates emotions of others, anticipates obstacles and stays focused on goals and makes decisions and takes action in uncertain situations and creates a backup plan.

Develop Networks
- This position builds trust to fairly represent every party, uses network to identify opportunities, establishes credibility and common purpose with a range of people, actively represents needs and varying groups, creates strategic impression by inspiring and connecting with values and beliefs.

Systems Thinking
- This position takes a long-term view towards organization’s objectives and how to achieve them, takes holistic long-term view of challenges and opportunities, anticipates outcomes and potential impacts, seeks stakeholder perspectives, works towards actions and plans aligned with APS values and works with others to identify areas for collaboration.

This link will assist you with understanding competencies.

Qualifications

Required:

A University graduation in a field related to the position assignment, supplemented by five years progressively responsible experience.
CPA or legacy designation (CA, CMA, CGA).
Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis.

Assets

Relevant legislation, regulations and policies, specifically the Financial Administration Act, Government Accountability Act, Government Organization Act, Fiscal Responsibility Act, Treasury Board Directives, etc.
Demonstrated experience with financial operations and management within a public sector environment.
Government strategic and policy directions as they relate to the Ministry's mandate and initiatives.
Ministry business plans, programs, deliverables and initiatives and related financial issues.
Strategic, business, operational, fiscal and human resource planning and accountability processes used in AE and GoA.
The political environment within which the Ministry operates and the decision-making processes of Government.
Clients and stakeholders affected by Ministry legislation, policies and initiatives, including relevant committees, advisory groups and senior representatives.
Best practices associated with financial accountability, continuous improvement and quality assurance.
Thorough knowledge of business-related software and automated financial systems.

Minimum recruitment standards outline the minimum education and experience required for appointments to a job classification.

Notes

Hours of Work – 36.25 hours per week (full time), Monday to Friday.

Term of Employment – Full-time

Location – ATB Place North, Edmonton

Candidates may be considered on a secondment basis, subject to approval from their home position/department. There may be an opportunity for the appointment to be extended beyond the initial term.

jobs.description:
Senior Director, Finance – The Mustard Seed

This executive search is conducted by Nelson/Kraft & Associates on behalf of The Mustard Seed

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Mustard Seed is searching for a seasoned and collaborative financial leader with initiative and drive to join their team as Senior Director, Finance.
The Senior Director, Finance is the CFO’s principal operational finance leader and trusted second-in-command. The role provides enterprise leadership across accounting, financial reporting, grants, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, audit, internal controls, finance systems, and process improvement. The successful candidate combines deep Controller-level technical expertise with strong people leadership, sound judgment, and the ability to translate financial complexity into practical decisions that support The Mustard Seed’s mission and long-term sustainability.
If you are an experienced CPA and team leader who comes from a mid to large sized organization with similarly complex moving parts, we would love to hear from you!

WHO WE ARE

The Mustard Seed is a Christian humanitarian organization whose vision is to build community, grow hope, and support change. Intentionally following Jesus Christ and partnering with the community, The Mustard Seed combats the root causes of poverty in Alberta, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan and works to create positive, lasting change in the lives of those we serve. The Mustard Seed provides basic services (food, clothing, housing, and support services), education, and employment to those living in poverty in the locations we serve.

OUR HISTORY

Pat Nixon founded The Mustard Seed in 1984 with a single street ministry location in central Calgary. Today, the organization operates in multiple cities – Calgary, Edmonton, Red Deer, Medicine Hat, and Grande Prairie in Alberta, Kamloops in British Columbia, and Saskatoon in Saskatchewan. All locations offer a different range of programs and services to serve our most vulnerable community members.

Programs & Services Include:

Basic Needs – emergency shelter, meals, clothing and hygiene items
Health and Wellness
Housing
Employment
Spiritual Care
Community Engagement
Community Impact Centres

IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE

The ideal candidate is a senior CPA finance leader with deep Controller-level technical expertise and a successful record of leading finance functions in a complex, larger organization. They have personally led significant year-end audits, overseen accounting and financial reporting, managed grant-funded operations, strengthened internal controls, improved budgeting and forecasting, and led finance systems and process transformation. They are equally comfortable resolving a technical accounting issue, guiding a manager, challenging a budget assumption, working with auditors and funders, and advising the CFO and Executive Team. The successful candidate will provide dependable operational leadership while helping modernize Finance and strengthen The Mustard Seed’s financial sustainability, stewardship, and organizational capacity.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Professional Designations, Required

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation in good standing.
Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, commerce, business administration, or a related discipline.
Ongoing professional development in accounting standards, financial reporting, governance, internal controls, audit, risk management, and finance leadership.

Preferred Assets

CRMA, CFE, CIA, or another relevant risk, controls, audit, fraud, or governance designation.
Advanced training or certification in ERP systems, data analytics, business intelligence, financial systems implementation, finance transformation, or project management.

Experience Requirements

Approximately 12 to 15+ years of progressive finance and accounting experience, including significant senior leadership responsibility.
A minimum of 5 to 7 years of leading managers and professional finance teams in a large or larger mid-sized, complex organization.
Significant experience serving in a Controller, Corporate Controller, or equivalent senior controllership role, with accountability for the integrity of financial reporting, accounting operations, internal controls, and close processes.
Extensive experience leading the annual external audit from planning through completion, including audit schedules, working papers, issue resolution, management responses, and relationships with external auditors and governance committees.
Demonstrated leadership across financial reporting, general accounting, grants accounting, budgeting and forecasting, treasury, internal controls, risk management, and audit coordination.
Substantial experience with grant-funded operations, including grant budgeting, restricted funding, contribution agreements, eligible expenditures, cost allocations, claims, financial reporting, compliance, funder audits, and closeout.
Experience leading finance systems and process improvement, including ERP optimization or implementation, systems integration, reporting automation, data quality, business intelligence, and finance workflow redesign.
Experience building, restructuring, developing, or stabilizing a finance function while maintaining reliable day-to-day delivery.
Experience advising executives and presenting clear, decision-focused financial information to senior leadership and governance bodies.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in a large charity, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector, social services, affordable housing, or similarly complex mission-driven environment.
Experience managing a large portfolio of municipal, provincial, federal, or other government funding agreements.
Deep practical experience with fund accounting, restricted contributions, contribution revenue recognition, capital projects, and government-funded initiatives.
Experience with Salesforce-based ERP environments such as Certinia/FinancialForce, budgeting and forecasting tools, Tableau or similar BI platforms, and broader data governance initiatives.

Calgary, AB

November 27, 2026

: $125,000-$130,000

Job Information

Job Title: Director, Financial Operations & Projects

Job Requisition ID: 89324

Ministry: Advanced Education

Location: Edmonton

Full or Part-Time: Full Time

Hours of Work: 36.25 hours per week

Permanent/Temporary/Wage: Permanent

Scope: Open Competition

Closing Date: November 30, 2026

Classification: Senior Manager Zone 2

Salary: $5,139.30 to $6,526.16 bi-weekly ($134,135- $170,333/year)

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Ministry Of Advanced Education

The Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta is responsible for overseeing the post-secondary education system. It plays a vital role in supporting universities, colleges, polytechnic institutions, and apprenticeship programs across the province.

In addition, the Ministry works to align education with the needs of Alberta’s economy by promoting skills development, research, and innovation. It collaborates with educational institutions, industry partners, and communities to prepare students for successful careers and to contribute to the province’s economic and social growth.

Overall, the Ministry of Advanced Education plays a critical role in shaping Alberta’s future by strengthening its workforce and supporting lifelong learning opportunities for all residents.

To learn more about the Ministry of Advanced Education in Alberta and what it has to offer, follow this link: Advanced Education | Alberta.ca

Role Responsibilities

Reporting to the Executive Director, Financial Services, the Director, Financial Operations & Projects, leads and continuously improves the Ministry’s financial and procurement operations, systems, and processes to support strategic business objectives.

Working in a complex and evolving environment, the Director manages competing priorities, develops innovative solutions, and adapts strategies to achieve results. The role requires strong leadership, problem-solving, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills to balance interests and build consensus.

The Director provides advice and guidance to senior management, executives, the Deputy Minister, and the Minister, influencing decisions and ensuring alignment between Ministry and Government priorities. Sound judgement, diplomacy, and the ability to navigate politically and financially sensitive issues are essential.

Job Responsilbilites

Lead the Financial Operations & Projects team in the review of current systems, processes and procedures with a Save view to assessing the potential risk of the current controls and providing options for the enhancements that could be implemented to strengthen the financial controls protecting Ministry assets as well as protecting the integrity of its financial reporting controls.
Work with program areas across the department to support procurement and contracting by assessing risks, providing alternatives and identifying business solutions that meet program area needs within the parameters of prudent business and government policies and trade agreements.
Recommend options and actions to improve affordability, value for money, and alignment with government priorities.
Develop ministry-wide financial operation processes to facilitate the efficient and effective delivery of department business.
Develop innovative approaches to new and existing financial systems, and support program financial teams.
Ensure all Ministry users have access to the required automated tools and privileges to perform their duties effectively and efficiently while balancing internal controls and segregation of duties.
Manage human resource issues (e.g., recruitment, performance management, professional development plans, and supervision).
Promote a cooperative attitude between Financial Services and program areas to ensure that the review of internal controls are completed to improve the financial and procurement processes and reduce risk in the programs and divisions of the Ministry.
Provide financial advice and guidance to all levels of line management throughout the Ministry, assisting them to resolve complex management issues and ensuring that they comply with Treasury Board, Service Alberta and internal AE policies.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Drive for Results
- The position takes and delegates responsibility for outcomes, uses variety of resources to monitor own performance standards, acknowledges even indirect responsibility, commits to what is good for Albertans even if not immediately accepted and reaches goals consistent with APS direction.

Creative Problem Solving
- The position engages the community and resources at hand to address issues, engages perspective to seek root causes, finds ways to improve complex systems, employs resources from other areas to solve problems and engages others and encourages debate and idea generation to solve problems while addressing risks.

Agility
- The position identifies and manages required change and the associated risks, identifies alternative approaches and supports others to do the same, proactively explains impact of changes, anticipates and mitigates emotions of others, anticipates obstacles and stays focused on goals and makes decisions and takes action in uncertain situations and creates a backup plan.

Develop Networks
- This position builds trust to fairly represent every party, uses network to identify opportunities, establishes credibility and common purpose with a range of people, actively represents needs and varying groups, creates strategic impression by inspiring and connecting with values and beliefs.

Systems Thinking
- This position takes a long-term view towards organization’s objectives and how to achieve them, takes holistic long-term view of challenges and opportunities, anticipates outcomes and potential impacts, seeks stakeholder perspectives, works towards actions and plans aligned with APS values and works with others to identify areas for collaboration.

This link will assist you with understanding competencies.

Qualifications

Required:

A University graduation in a field related to the position assignment, supplemented by five years progressively responsible experience.
CPA or legacy designation (CA, CMA, CGA).
Related experience or education may be considered as an equivalency on a one for one basis.

Assets

Relevant legislation, regulations and policies, specifically the Financial Administration Act, Government Accountability Act, Government Organization Act, Fiscal Responsibility Act, Treasury Board Directives, etc.
Demonstrated experience with financial operations and management within a public sector environment.
Government strategic and policy directions as they relate to the Ministry's mandate and initiatives.
Ministry business plans, programs, deliverables and initiatives and related financial issues.
Strategic, business, operational, fiscal and human resource planning and accountability processes used in AE and GoA.
The political environment within which the Ministry operates and the decision-making processes of Government.
Clients and stakeholders affected by Ministry legislation, policies and initiatives, including relevant committees, advisory groups and senior representatives.
Best practices associated with financial accountability, continuous improvement and quality assurance.
Thorough knowledge of business-related software and automated financial systems.
